title: fix: cli improvements to handle port forward correctly
body:
The issue was that kagent cli was trying to port forward before the installation and there was no port forward after installation. The k8s resources needed for port forward are added by installation so any port forward before that is useless and we have to do a port forward after the installation.

Also improved cli by adding messages so that if someone tries the commands either as arguments or on cli before installation, they are told to perform installation first.
author: harmindersinghk

comments.body: Hey, thanks so much for the contribution! I am pretty busy at KubeCon right now but will do my best to have a look tomorrow.

> I really appreciate this PR, but I think we need to take a small step-back and figure out if we can handle this at a higher level, either via lifecycle in the cli library, or lifecycle that we create. For example, if the connection check fails can we try and reconnect, rather than doing it from only the install command?

We are not doing it only from install command. Port-forward is set up in two places:

1. When you enter kagent shell. This is going to fail if install hasn't been done yet. No matter how many times you retry its going to fail as the resources to which we are port-forwarding are not there.Once install command is run, and we exit and enter the shell again this is going to work ok as we now have the resources.
2. When install command is run. This is done so that if someone doesn't exit and renters shell after install command the subsequent commands in the same shell still work.
Sorry you will have to rebase with main again.

title: feat(controller): add comprehensive logging to HTTP handlers
body:
This commit adds detailed logging to all REST API handlers in the controller:

- Add structured logging with context information (operation type, user ID, resource IDs)
- Implement different log levels (Info for important events, V(1) for detailed operations)
- Enhance error logging with detailed context
- Improve validation error messages in the team creation handler
- Create consistent logging patterns across all handlers
- Add logging to helper functions for complete traceability

The changes follow best practices by using request-scoped loggers that carry request context, allowing for better debugging and monitoring in production.

Fixes #203

author: bleggett

comments.body:
> This looks awesome, but I have 2 main comments:
> 
>     1. Where is the `proto` file for this located? I think there should be some sort of tooling to copy it and re-generate just in case that ever needs to happen.

Currently it resides in Solo's internal `ztunnel` repo. I'll add a make target/script to make the regen process more obvious.

>     2. We need to handle the case when this is running in cluster, when it's running in cluster we can just get endpoints and use those rather than port-forward which is pretty annoying.

Yeah the underlying API is primarily designed to be used from outside the cluster. It does not expose endpoints to the outside world, and only works with port-forwarding. AFAIK portforwarding used here should work just as well from inside the cluster as it does outside of it, and one nice thing about using portforwarding is that access to this endpoint can be controlled simply with k8s RBAC - if for instance you had specific workloads you wanted to make inaccessible to inspection by the agent (or anyone/anything else)

At least, since other tools here also use `kubectl` I assume we have client creds available already.
Closing for now
